summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Tom Allen beat J. C. Gallagher in sixteen rounds on a small island near the arsenal, a secretly arranged fight seen by only 40 or 50 people after the Kansas plan was put out as a decoy.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'The Missouri Republican, Sunday Morning, November 6, 1870'. The paper was not the St. Louis Republic until 1888.

facts.fact: Allen defeated J. C. Gallagher on a small island near the arsenal; Gallagher's sponge was thrown up when the 17th round was called, after 16 rounds and 26 1/2 minutes
places: Island near the arsenal, St. Louis

facts.fact: The fight was for $1,500 stakes, $1,000 put up by Allen against Gallagher's $500
Allen was seconded by Barney Aaron and George Collins; Gallagher by Mike McCoole and Tom Kelly

notes: Fight came off 'early yesterday morning' (Saturday 1870-11-05). Party left from the boat Bertha at the foot of Barton street.
